# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 16 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 8

**1** When she had finished she asked me, "Is there anything more you want to ask?" I said, "Lady, why is the tower built upon water?" She replied, "Because your life has been saved and will be saved through water. But the tower has been founded upon the word of the almighty and glorious Name, and it is upheld by the invisible power of the Lord." **2** "That is wonderful, lady. But who are the six young men who are building it?" "These are the holy angels of God who were created first, to whom the Lord delivered all his creation to build up, increase, and govern. Through them the building of the tower will be completed." **3** "And the other people who bring the stones?" "These also are holy angels of God, but the six are over them. When the building is completed, all will rejoice together around the tower and glorify God, because the tower is finished." **4** I asked, "Lady, I want to understand the rejected stones near the tower, the ones thrown far away, and the cracked ones." **5** She replied: "The stones rejected but left near the tower are those who have sinned and wish to repent. They have not been thrown far because they will be useful in the building if they repent. **6** If they repent, they will be strong and incorporated into the building — but only if they repent now while the tower is still being built. When the tower is completed there will be no more room, and they will be cast aside." **7** "The cracked ones are those who have faith but also hold worldly wealth. When tribulation comes, they deny the Lord on account of their riches and business dealings." "When will they be useful for the building, lady?" "When their misleading wealth is stripped away from them, they will be useful to God. For just as a round stone cannot become square unless it is cut and loses something of itself, so those who are rich cannot be useful to God unless their riches are cut away from them." **8** "Lady, I also want to know about the white round ones that did not fit the building — who are they?" She replied, "How long will you be slow to understand, asking about everything and grasping nothing? These are those who have faith but also hold the riches of this age. When tribulation comes, they deny their Lord on account of their wealth and business dealings."

---

### Council Notes

This chapter contains a significant repetition and conflation of material from ch. 7-8. Scholars recognize this as evidence of the Shepherd's composite literary character — different versions of the tower allegory, now preserved side by side.

The anti-wealth theology is strikingly consistent: the wealthy appear in three separate categories (cracked stones, round stones, white round stones) — all variations on the same problem. Wealth is not simply a disadvantage; it is an impediment to the very shape that God's building requires.

The water/word duality in v. 1 is the Shepherd's most succinct ecclesiology: the Church is sustained by baptism AND by the divine Name — the sacramental and the theological together.
